authoredFrom: BD-lines: the state the lane shipped in. The string `line_number` occurred ZERO times in the analyzer, so every json edge in the index carried a NULL line while symbols carried `range` throughout - the position was known and simply not published. Every row pins `line_number` explicitly, so a mutant that strips the field cannot pass: the matcher requires the key present AND equal. Also pins that a nested key is owned by its parent SYMBOL (`nested`) and not by its qualified path (`Lines.nested`) - the same defect one level down, invisible at the top level. `contains` endpoints are QUALIFIED PATHS: this pin set was migrated from bare-name endpoints by a structure-preserving transformation (owner and child and line unchanged, spelling resolved against the fixture's own qualifiedName). The reason is measured, not stylistic: over a 202-file, 99-repo sample 32,660 of 66,032 `contains` edges (49.4%) named a target matching MORE THAN ONE published symbol, and the shared resolver declines a non-unique bare name, so those edges bound to no declaration at all. See meta.endpoints=qualified_path on the edge.
